newsitem.title: SOMALIA: Somali group says it repulsed Ethiopian attack.
newsitem.headline: Somali group says it repulsed Ethiopian attack.

text.p: A Moslem fundamentalist group said on Monday it had repulsed an attack by Ethiopian troops on one of its bases in western Somalia and killed three Ethiopian soldiers.
Ahmed Bile, secretary of the al-Ittihad al-Islam group, told reporters in Mogadishu Ethiopian troops crossed into Somalia on Sunday and attacked Dolow town, 500 km (300 miles) southwest of Mogadishu.
He said al-Ittihad fighters defended their base at Dolow and both sides fought with machineguns, anti-aircraft batteries, mortars and anti-tank rockets for 90 minutes.
Another al-Ittihad official, Hassan Dahir Awies, said the attackers were repulsed, three Ethiopian soldiers were killed, a number were wounded and some weapons were captured on Sunday.
He said one al-Ittihad fighter was wounded in the attack.
There was no independent confirmation of Ethiopian military involvement and no comment from the Ethiopian capital Addis Ababa.

Aid officials said they were checking reports from residents of the region that a rival Somali faction, the Somali National Front (SNF) from Dolow, attacked al-Ittihad militiamen in Beled Hawa town to the south on Sunday and had been beaten back.
Other reports reaching Mogadishu by radio from Gedo also said only the SNF and al-Ittihad were involved in the fighting.

"We have heard of no Ethiopian involvement but it looks like the SNF on Sunday tried to take back Beled Hawa from al-Ittihad and were repulsed. We hear one from each side was killed," an official said.

Ethiopia mounted a two-day incursion into Somalia last month against the Moslem fundamentalists, whom Ethiopia blamed for recent bomb attacks in Addis Ababa. It said the attacks were directed against the fundamentalists' bases and training camps.

The Ethiopians seized control of three towns including Dolow and Beled Hawa before withdrawing. Ethiopian officials said their forces might return for more attacks against what they called a "multinational terrorist group" operating from Somalia.
Al-Ittihad said its forces killed at least 150 Ethiopian soldiers while resisting last month's attack. The group said it also downed an Ethiopian helicopter and destroyed a tank.
The incursion prompted al-Ittihad to send reinforcements from Mogadishu to Gedo and its other bases in western Somalia.
